findings.title: Second `downsize` definition silently replaces the width/height version
findings.body:
`OptimizedImage.downsize` is now defined twice. Ruby keeps only the last definition, `downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})`, so the `(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` variant at line 145 is dead code.

Existing callers that pass width and height separately will break:
- With 5 arguments (`from, to, w, h, opts`) they raise `ArgumentError`.
- With 4 arguments the height integer is treated as `opts`, so `opts[:allow_animation]` raises a `TypeError` on an Integer.

One example is upload/avatar downsizing that uses `max_image_width`/`max_image_height`. Give the percentage variant a different name (e.g. `downsize_by`), or have a single method that accepts either form.

findings.title: `tempfile.size` may not reflect the file rewritten in place
findings.body:
The loop runs `convert`/ImageOptim with `tempfile.path` as both source and target, then re-checks `tempfile.size`.

`Tempfile#size` stats the already-open file descriptor. If the tools replace the file (write a new file and rename it over the path, as ImageOptim does), the descriptor still points at the old inode and reports the original size. Two consequences:
- The loop can keep shrinking the image all 5 times (down to about 33% linear size) even after it already fits.
- `Upload.create_for` receives a stale filesize.

Use `File.size(tempfile.path)` instead. Also note that the result of `downsize` (success or failure) is ignored.

findings.title: Animated GIF downsizing passes a percentage to gifsicle
findings.body:
When `allow_animated_thumbnails` is on and the file is a GIF, `downsize_instructions_animated` produces `gifsicle --resize-fit 80%`. gifsicle's `--resize-fit` expects `WxH`, not a percentage, so the command fails every time. The loop retries 5 times uselessly and the oversized GIF is then rejected.

When animations are off, `convert from[0]` keeps only the first frame, so animated GIFs are silently flattened to a still image just because they were large.

findings.title: In-place downsizing depends on the tempfile having a correct extension
findings.body:
`convert` picks the output format from the target path's extension, and the GIF check matches on `from`. The tempfile from `FileHelper.download` (the API URL path) may not carry the original image extension. In that case the conversion may fail or write an unexpected format.

SVG also matches `is_image?` and would be run through ImageMagick rasterization with an `.svg` output path. Consider skipping vector formats and ensuring the tempfile path keeps the right extension.

findings.title: Client-side size limit hard-coded to 10MB for all upload types
findings.body:
`validateUploadedFile` now ignores `max_attachment_size_kb` (and `max_image_size_kb`) and always allows up to 10MB. Server-side downsizing only applies to images, so non-image attachments larger than the configured limit now pass the client check, get uploaded, and are rejected only after the full transfer.

The 10MB value is also duplicated as a magic number in two places and in `uploads_controller.rb`. Keep the per-type setting for attachments and make the image ceiling a single shared setting.
